_comment: AI neural network and PPO hyperparameters. All tunable constants live here, not hardcoded - mirrors physics.json/attributes.json pattern.

action._comment_arm_tackle_without_carrier: true = a sampled tackle_attempt ALWAYS sets player.tackle_armed (unless the player is knocked down), even when no opponent has the ball -- so the armed-tackle cost is paid for every attempt (x tackle_armed_while_possessing_multiplier while holding the ball) and the attempt bonus still only pays when an armed tackle resolves contact (the engine only resolves an armed tackle against an opposing carrier in range). Lets a player pre-arm and run into the tackle as the ball arrives, while making pointless arming cost something. false = old behaviour: an attempt with no opposing carrier is a free, unarmed 'tackle_no_carrier' no-op (measured on run293: 96% of sampled tackles were such no-ops, the head fired 37% of the time while the trainee held the ball and 3% while the opponent did).
action._comment_kick_one_shot: true = one kick decision fires at most one kick: once the kick a decision asked for has executed (in-possession kick on the decision tick, or an armed kick auto-firing on first touch), NeuralPlayerAI stops re-applying it for the rest of the decision interval. false = old behaviour: the cached decision is re-applied every tick, so an in-possession kick re-armed and re-fired after the ball was released (measured on run293: ~3 physical kicks per decision, kick_armed set at the interval boundary in 96% of cases -> the armed-kick cost was charged to ordinary possession kicks). Fired armed kicks still pay the armed cost and earn the attempt bonus (see ScenarioEnv._compute_phase1_reward_for_player).

logging._comment_consistency_interval_s: How often the match logger emits a 'consistency' snapshot entry when no other events have fired (seconds of sim time).

eval._comment_pre_ppo_eval_enabled: train.py only: whether to run the 4 pre-PPO evals (vs rules-based AI, vs immobile, self-play, rules-vs-rules baseline) after pre-training but before PPO starts. Only takes effect when --pre-ppo-eval-trials is NOT passed on the CLI -- an explicit --pre-ppo-eval-trials (0 or otherwise) always overrides this. false = skip all 4 entirely, matching --pre-ppo-eval-trials 0. These evals have no effect on training itself (informational only) and no downstream dependency: skipping them doesn't change the separate, lazily-cached rules-vs-rules baseline computed during training for the '[eval baseline rules-vs-rules]'/gap= numbers.
eval._comment: Seeded evaluation, shared by PPOTrainer._eval_vs_rules() (pre-training + every rollout) and evaluate.py -- see ai/eval/seeded_eval.py. eval_n_seeds fixed scenario seeds starting at eval_seed_base are reused identically every eval call, so results are comparable across an entire run instead of noise from a fresh random scenario draw each time. eval_repeats_per_seed re-runs each seed that many times (averaged into the same aggregate stats) to reduce residual match-physics/PPO-sampling noise without growing the scenario set. eval_n_parallel_workers >1 spawns that many subprocesses (mirrors ppo.n_processes); this does NOT seed PPO training itself, only evaluation call sites.
eval._comment_swap_sides: Field-side fairness for every seeded eval in this file (vs-rules, vs-immobile, rules-vs-rules baseline, neural-snapshot comparisons): when true, each seed is ALSO run a second time with ai/eval/seeded_eval.py's swap_player_states() applied right after the scenario is built -- trainee and opponent's full state (team, attributes, position, velocity, heading, stamina) is swapped between them, while player_id (and therefore which network/AI drives 'trainee') stays fixed. This means 'trainee' experiences BOTH roles that seed's random draw produced across the two passes, canceling out any positional/attribute advantage tied to one specific role. Deliberately a separate flag from eval_repeats_per_seed (which keeps meaning exactly 'episodes per seed per side') rather than folding this in -- true doubles total eval episode count.
eval._comment_batched_eval: When true, every seeded eval in this file (vs-rules, vs-immobile, rules-vs-rules baseline, neural-snapshot comparisons) batches its episodes' decision-network calls across eval_envs_per_process envs at a time per worker process, via ai/eval/seeded_eval.py's run_seeded_evaluation_batched -- the same amortized-dispatch-overhead speedup ppo.batched_rollout gives real rollout collection (see that key's comment), applied to evaluation. False (default) = unchanged: each worker runs its assigned episodes one at a time (batch-of-1 network calls) via run_seeded_evaluation. Neural-vs-neural snapshot eval also batches the opponent's decisions (a second _sample_action_batch call per round, using the frozen snapshot's own weights) when this is true -- rules/immobile opponents have no neural decision to batch either way.
eval._comment_neural_snapshot: Neural-vs-neural self-eval (PPOTrainer._maybe_run_neural_snapshot_eval): every neural_snapshot_eval_every_n_rollouts rollouts, compare the CURRENT live policy against the checkpoint saved neural_snapshot_lookbacks[i] rollouts ago, for EVERY entry in that list, plus 'original' (this run's checkpoint1.pt) -- on the same eval_seeds/eval_repeats_per_seed budget as the vs-rules/vs-immobile evals above. Reads the checkpoint FILES _save_checkpoint() already writes every rollout (checkpoint_dir/checkpoint{N}.pt) rather than keeping a separate in-memory snapshot -- no extra memory cost, and an INTEGER entry ('K rollouts back') is just checkpoint{current_count-K}.pt. A FLOAT entry (e.g. 0.5) instead names a FRACTION of the run's checkpoint count so far (see _resolve_snapshot_lookback): 0.5 always compares against the checkpoint sitting at the run's current halfway point, a target that moves forward as current_count grows, unlike a fixed lookback -- useful for a 'how far have I come since the middle of this run' signal that stays meaningful at any run length, instead of one particular fixed distance becoming irrelevant once the run is much longer than it. The label keeps the configured fraction ('0.5_back'), not the drifting checkpoint number, so it groups consistently in logs/graphs. Requires checkpoint_dir to be set (train.py always sets one); a lookback with not-yet-enough history is silently skipped until enough checkpoints accumulate. neural_snapshot_eval_every_n_rollouts=0 disables the whole feature (no extra eval run, zero added cost). This is the ONLY way to get a genuinely paired 'did the policy actually improve' signal, since PPO's own noisy training rollouts mix real improvement with random episode-mix variance -- comparing against fixed past selves on fixed seeds isolates the former.

observation._comment_max_task_ids: Width of the GlobalFeatures task-id one-hot (scaffolding, see ai/knowledge.md 'Task-id: scaffolded, not yet load-bearing'). Must match schema.py's MAX_TASK_IDS.
observation._comment_sim_dt_s: Physics tick size. Default 0.0333 (30Hz). Increase for faster training: 0.05=20Hz (~1.5x), 0.067=15Hz (~2x). UI ignores this and always uses 30Hz.
observation._comment_ball_spin_nn_norm_rad_s: NOT a physical spin limit -- a normalization/scale constant for feeding spin to neural nets. Shared between two systems: (1) ai/obs/encoder.py's live-match spin normalization scale (and ai/ppo/bc.py's kick_spin BC loss, which reads this same key -- see bc.py's _SPIN_NN_NORM_RAD_S), and (2) physics_pretrain.ball's sampling-range upper bound for _sample_spin (ball_episode_gen.py) -- how strong a spin CAN be drawn for a synthetic episode. It is NOT physics_pretrain's dataset normalization divisor -- that's the separate, deliberately hardcoded BALL_SPIN_NORM_DIVISOR_RAD_S (=30.0) constant in ball_episode_gen.py, chosen so widening this sampling range doesn't retroactively change how already-generated dataset shards encode spin (ball_dataset.generate_dataset APPENDS to existing shards rather than overwriting, so a drifting divisor would silently mix incompatible normalizations across shards). Both direct readers of this key (encoder.py, bc.py) load it via ai_config at import/call time rather than hardcoding a copy, so there is nothing else to update by hand when this value changes.
observation._comment_time: Use log1p normalization for time_remaining to spread out the low end (see ai_design_doc.md section 7.5)

network._comment_inter_player_attn_heads: Heads for the inter-player self-attention pass that runs over other-player embeddings BEFORE the main query step. Divisors of entity_embed_dim (45): 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. 0 = disabled. No-op in 1v1; becomes useful for 2v2+ where player-player relational context matters.
network._comment_share_entity_encoder: If true, ExecutionNetwork reuses DecisionNetwork's entity_encoder, ball_mlp, and global_mlp (same nn.Module objects, shared weights + shared gradient). Halves encoder computation per decision tick. Set false to give each network fully independent encoders.
network._comment_exec_trunk_hidden: Trunk hidden dim for the main policy ExecutionNetwork. null = fall back to trunk_hidden. Set a smaller int (e.g. 96) to reduce execution network capacity and rely more on the decision latent.
network._comment_value_net_trunk_hidden: Optional override for trunk_hidden used ONLY by the dedicated separate value network (trainer.value_net, see ppo.__init__ 'separate_value_net' / CLI --separate-value-net). null (default) = same size as the main trunk_hidden above. Set an int (e.g. 96 for a smaller/cheaper critic, or 384 for a bigger one) to size the standalone critic's trunk independently of the shared policy trunk -- has NO effect at all when --separate-value-net is not passed (the main execution_net always uses trunk_hidden).
network._comment_value_hidden_dim: Hidden layer size for value_head (critic). 0 = old behaviour, a single Linear(trunk_hidden+value_extra_hidden, 1) with no nonlinearity. >0 inserts one Linear+ReLU hidden layer before the final scalar output, giving the critic its own nonlinear capacity instead of relying purely on a linear readout of the shared (policy) trunk. Try 32-128; raise if value RMSE plateaus well above 0 while train loss for the policy looks fine.
network._comment_value_dropout: Dropout probability applied ONLY inside value_head (ExecutionNetwork), immediately before each Linear layer -- never touches the shared trunk `h` that also feeds the policy/motor heads, so it cannot destabilise action distributions. 0.0 (default) = disabled. Standard dropout range for a small regression head like this is roughly 0.1-0.3; useful if the critic is overfitting a small/reused offline dataset (train loss falling while val loss rises). Note: nn.Dropout auto-disables under .eval() but PPO rollout action-sampling does NOT call .eval() on execution_net, so a nonzero value also lightly perturbs the value estimate used for GAE bootstrapping during rollout collection -- harmless (value isn't used to pick actions) but worth knowing if val= jitter increases after enabling.
network._comment_physics_encoder_checkpoints: Opt-in wiring of the frozen, standalone-pretrained ball/player dynamics encoders (ai/physics_pretrain/, see agent_plans/ball_physics_pretrain_plan.md section 8) into the main policy networks. null (default) = feature off, ball_dim/self_dim stay exactly BALL_FEATURE_DIM/PLAYER_FEATURE_DIM, byte-identical behaviour to before this feature existed. Set a path (e.g. 'checkpoints/physics_pretrain/ball_encoder_68.midtrain_latest.pt') to concatenate that checkpoint's frozen latent + auxiliary-head outputs onto ball_feat/self_feat/other_feat before they reach ball_mlp/self_mlp/entity_encoder -- see ai/knowledge.md 'Frozen physics-dynamics encoders'. Only DecisionNetwork loads/owns the encoder; ExecutionNetwork reads the precomputed result off DecisionHeadsRaw instead of recomputing (see decision_network.py/execution_network.py forward()). Enabling this for a run makes ball_mlp's/self_mlp's/entity_encoder's first-layer weights a different shape -- an existing checkpoint trained WITHOUT this set will fail to load into a trainer built WITH it set (and vice versa); this does not affect recorded .npz BC datasets (the observation schema itself never changes).
network._comment: Shared-trunk actor/critic (Option A from section 9.4). Switch to separate trunk if value loss destabilises policy.

ppo._comment_dual_clip_c: Dual-clip PPO (Ye et al. 2020, 'Mastering Complex Control in MOBA Games with Deep Reinforcement Learning' -- the OpenAI Five/Tencent lineage), opt-in. Vanilla PPO's clip only bounds the surrogate objective for POSITIVE advantage; for NEGATIVE advantage, if ratio blows up (network drastically increases the probability of an action its own advantage estimate says was bad), the unclipped side keeps decreasing without bound as ratio grows, giving an UNBOUNDED positive policy_loss contribution from that one row -- confirmed live in training_runs.md's recurring '[ratio spike]' negative-adv entries implying per-sample policy_loss in the hundreds to (rarely) tens of thousands. This adds a second floor, ONLY for adv<0: max(min(surr1,surr2), dual_clip_c*adv) -- bounds that row's worst case at dual_clip_c*|adv| without touching the already-fine positive-advantage path at all. 0.0 (default, falsy) disables entirely -- byte-identical to vanilla PPO. When enabled, use a value > 1 (paper/typical practice: 2.0-3.0) -- see PPOTrainer.__init__'s dual_clip_c comment for why it should exceed 1+clip_range.
ppo._comment_decision_value_coef: Only used with --separate-value-net --share-value-grad-with-decision. Scales the slice of self.value_net's gradient that reaches decision_net specifically (main PPO update loop only -- see ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'Separate value network'). Deliberately separate from vf_coef, which keeps scaling value_loss's contribution to value_net's own trunk unchanged regardless of this.
ppo._comment_ent_coef_20260924: Raised 0.002 -> 0.003 (1.5x) for the run310 -> run311 restart: kick_dir/kick_power both fully saturated by the end of run310 (entropy went slightly negative -- kappa~41, kick_power sigma~0.125), and the per-head 'only' boosts alone weren't holding them back. Rather than just raising those two further in isolation, the base coefficient goes up for every head, with ent_move_dir_weight compensated (5.5 -> 4.0, via 1+(5.5-1)*0.002/0.003 -- the boost term is additive as (weight-1)*raw, per that weight's own comment, not a plain multiplier, so a straight /1.5 would over-cut it) to hold move_dir's NET pressure roughly where it was -- that head was behaving fine (steady kappa growth, no collapse) and doesn't need more push. ent_kick_weight is deliberately NOT cut to compensate, even though it's also a 'behaving fine' head in isolation -- see its own comment: it's a SHARED multiplier across the kick gate AND kick_dir/kick_power's base entropy (before the 'only' boosts), so cutting it would partially undo the extra kick_dir/kick_power pressure this change is trying to add. The kick gate riding along with the full 1.5x is an accepted side effect (its entropy has been flat/stable throughout, and kick_prob has been trending down, so slightly more exploration pressure there is neutral-to-helpful, not a concern). ent_kick_power_only_weight/ent_kick_dir_azimuth_only_weight (their own comments) are ADDITIONALLY raised on top of the 1.5x base rise, since those two heads specifically need more than a proportional share.
ppo._comment_grad_norm_spike_k: Diagnostic only -- does not affect training. Adaptive, not a fixed number: PPOTrainer keeps a rolling window (last 200 minibatches, pooled across PPO/BC/DAgger) of raw (pre-clip) grad norms, and whenever one exceeds (running_mean + grad_norm_spike_k * running_std) of that window, logs a per-parameter-tensor breakdown (top params by norm, across BOTH decision_net and execution_net including encoders/trunk, not just per-execution-head like the existing [exec head grad norm] summary) for that ONE minibatch, to help identify which specific layer is driving an outlier step. null disables the check entirely. Adaptive because 'typical scale' varies a lot by run/config -- a fixed absolute number tuned for one run's mean~5/max~200 wrongly stayed silent on a smaller run's mean~4.6/max~14.3 outlier, which was still ~3.9 standard deviations out (k=5 also missed that specific case -- ~3.85sigma < 5sigma bar -- hence k=4.0 as the default). k=4.0 means 'more than 4 std above this run's own recent average' -- requires at least 20 samples in the window before checking at all (too little history has a meaningless mean/std).
ppo._comment_learning_rate_20260923: All three cut 5e-5 -> 3e-5 (and ppg_lr to match, see bc.ppg_lr below) for the run309b -> run310 restart at 100M steps: user's hypothesis is the per-iteration jitter (loss/entropy/KL wobble visible in the graphs) is partly just LR-scale noise, not a signal worth chasing, and a lower LR should smooth it out without materially slowing progress. Untested -- watch whether iteration-to-iteration noise actually drops and whether progress (eval win%, kappa/sigma sharpening rate) slows disproportionately.
ppo._comment_n_epochs_20260924: 8 -> 10 for the next restart (run311 -> run312). Only takes effect on a fresh PPOTrainer construction (read once in __init__), so this does not affect the currently-running run311.
ppo._comment_lr_warmup_steps: Linear LR warmup over the first N optimizer steps of EVERY PPO update (each rollout's update starts from ratio=1/KL=0, and Adam's first steps into the new batch overshoot). Step k (0-based) runs at (k+1)/N of that update's scheduled lr (all param groups, incl. value); full lr from step N-1 on. 0 = off (constant scheduled lr). Same idea as bc.ppg_warmup_steps, which was tuned offline for the PPG refit (25-50 steps removed its early-KL bump); the right N for PPO itself is untested. Applies to the main PPO minibatch step only (not value-only/BC continuation passes, not the separate value net's optimizer).
ppo._comment_val_episode_fraction: Diagnostic only -- never affects training/early-stopping. Fraction of each rollout's COMPLETE episodes (segmented per track_id, so a batched secondary neural opponent's interleaved rows can never straddle the split) to randomly hold out from every PPO minibatch update this call, then re-evaluate (forward pass only) under the current weights at the end of every epoch -- logged as 'val_episode_policy_loss='/'val_episode_value_loss=' alongside the existing 'pol_mean='/'val_mean=' training-loss line in _ppo_update. 0.0 (default) disables entirely: no split, every row trains, byte-identical behaviour to before this existed. Needs at least 2 complete episodes in the rollout or the split is skipped for that update (everything trains that call). See PPOTrainer.__init__'s val_episode_fraction comment and _split_train_val_episodes()/_eval_val_episode_losses().
ppo._comment_log_epoch_zero_baseline: Diagnostic only. When true, logs one extra '== epoch 0 (pre-training baseline, ratio=1 exactly) ==' block per rollout, in the EXACT same [policy]/[policy surrogate]/[policy percentiles]/[policy heads]/[value] (and held-out equivalents) format as every real per-epoch block -- evaluated under CURRENT weights before epoch 1's first gradient step touches anything, so old_log_prob==new_log_prob exactly and policy_loss/KL/surrogate read trivially ~0 by construction (expected, not a bug), while value/percentiles/per-head numbers are real and give a clean before/after-epoch-1 comparison point. Costs one extra full no-grad forward pass over the whole rollout batch (and a second over val_batch when val_episode_fraction is also enabled) every rollout -- false (default) skips this entirely, byte-identical to before this existed. Meant to be flipped on temporarily to compare a few rollouts against a known-clean baseline, not left on permanently.
ppo._comment_value_pretrain_chunk_steps: Rows collected (per worker process) between whole-episode flushes when value_pretrain_batched_rollout is true; 0 = one big send at the end (the old, spikier RAM profile). Each flush sends only COMPLETED episodes (per env) and keeps each env's unfinished tail, so MC returns stay exact and the train/val episode split stays clean -- episodes are never cut at a flush boundary (see batched_rollout_worker.py 'Chunked streaming'). Workers also compute returns and pack the batch themselves and ship compact numpy arrays, and the main process ingests each chunk as it arrives, so peak RAM at the end of a rollout is bounded by a chunk plus the final tensors instead of several full copies at once. If a flush is due but no env has finished an episode yet, it just retries next round. Smaller = lower per-process memory but more messages; the default is fine for ~50-step episodes.
ppo._comment_bernoulli_reset_scale: Used only by --reset-bernoullis (train.py). Each of exec_move_logit/sprint_logit/kick_logit/tackle_attempt_logit (ExecutionNetwork's 4 Bernoulli action heads) is a single nn.Linear(trunk_hidden, 1); multiplying that layer's weight AND bias by this scale scales every logit it produces by the same factor, preserving sign -- scale<1 pulls p toward 0.5 (max entropy/exploration, i.e. flattening), scale>1 sharpens it (pushes existing confidence further from 0.5), scale=1.0 is a no-op. Input-dependent structure is preserved either way, unlike zeroing the layer outright which would destroy it. This is the Bernoulli-head analogue of --reset-dir-log-std/--reset-kick-power-log-std for the Gaussian/von-Mises heads (those reset a learned log_std/log_kappa scalar; there is no equivalent scalar here since a Bernoulli head has no separate spread parameter -- the logit magnitude itself IS the confidence -- so we scale the weights/bias directly instead, per user request/idea).
ppo._comment_kick_power_floor: Lower bound of the executed kick power fraction: power = floor + (1 - floor) * sigmoid(raw) (SquashedNormalHead low=floor, high=1). 0.0 = the old plain sigmoid. Physical meaning: ball speed = (12 + 12.3*kick_power_attr) m/s * power, i.e. ~19 m/s * power at attribute 0.6 -> 0.01 is ~0.2 m/s (a touch), 0.03 ~0.6 m/s, 0.05 ~1 m/s. Added so a policy that finds kicks disadvantageous cannot neutralise them by driving power to ~0 while keeping p(kick) (which also starves the kick direction/power heads of signal) -- every kick now has at least this much effect. PPO's log_prob/entropy/KL are on the raw draw, so they are unaffected; only the executed power (and BC's kick_power targets, via bc._kick_power_physical) use the floor. apply_nn_action.py now RAISES on a kick decision with power <= 0/NaN instead of silently using 0.85. Changing this changes the executed power of an existing checkpoint for the same raw output (small values get lifted), so keep it consistent across a run/eval.
ppo._comment_ent_kick_weight: Extra multiplier on the KICK heads' entropy bonus in the PPO loss ONLY: the kick gate (Bernoulli), kick_dir and kick_power entropy terms (on top of ent_kick_power_weight and the ent_coef schedule) are scaled by this. 1.0 = old behaviour exactly. Added because the kick heads' entropy was collapsing within the first PPO iterations (kick_prob ~6% and falling) before their direction/power heads, which only see kick rows, had any data to learn from; with E[kick]-weighting the kick_dir/kick_power terms are already scaled by p(kick), so they need a large multiplier to matter. The logged `entropy=` and the per-head entropy breakdown stay UNBOOSTED (the boost is added only where the loss is built), so trend lines remain comparable across settings.
ppo._comment_log_action_opportunity_stats: Phase 1 of agent_plans/masked_action_training_plan.md (instrumentation only, no change to the loss). When true the env records, per decision interval, whether a kick / armed tackle COULD have taken effect (entities/action_opportunity.py) and attaches the flags to every neural transition, so the batch carries action/opp_kick, opp_kick_raw, fired_kick, opp_tack, opp_tack_raw, fired_tack, opp_partial and the trainer logs an [action opp] block (P(opportunity), P(fired | kick=1), P(kick=1 | opportunity), cross-head cut share, invariant-violation counters) every rollout. false (default) = no flags, byte-identical to before. Implied by mask_untriggered_actions.
ppo._comment_mask_untriggered_actions: Phase 3 of agent_plans/masked_action_training_plan.md. When true, the kick gate and tackle_attempt gate get policy-gradient / entropy signal ONLY on rows whose decision interval had an opportunity for that action (opp_kick / opp_tack; both gate values), and kick_dir / kick_power only on rows where a kick actually fired (fired_kick). The PPO ratio uses log-probs summed over exactly those masked heads (old and new sides identically). Requires the flags, so it also switches on their recording. PPG / consistency anchors and BC stay unmasked. false (default) = behaviour identical to before.
ppo._comment_mask_rescale_by_opportunity_rat: Only with mask_untriggered_actions. false (default) = masked heads simply receive fewer gradient rows (gradient scaled by P(opportunity) relative to unmasked). true = each masked head's policy-loss / entropy terms are divided by that head's batch-mean mask so the per-opportunity-row gradient magnitude matches the unmasked case (faster learning for rare tackle opportunities, more variance). See plan D9.
ppo._comment_action_opportunity_cross_head_c: Independence rule for the opportunity flags (entities/action_opportunity.py, plan I1): when both a kick opportunity and a tackle opportunity occur in one decision interval, only the one that comes FIRST counts (a fired kick can remove the tackle opportunity, a won tackle can create the kick opportunity, so the later one depends on the gate bit being trained). false = count both (biased; only for measuring the size of the effect -- the raw flags opp_kick_raw / opp_tack_raw are always recorded regardless).
ppo._comment_y_canonical: Opt-in y-canonical AI frame (ai/obs/y_canonical.py). When true every network forward mirrors rows whose observer is at y < 0 about the x-axis before the network sees them and mirrors the y-signed outputs back, so the policy is EXACTLY flip_y-equivariant by construction (the observer's own side, y >= 0, is the tie-break) and flip_y augmentation becomes redundant -- set augment_n_slot_shuffles to 0 alongside it (a warning is logged otherwise). Checkpoint keys are unchanged (state_dict is delegated), but a checkpoint trained without it is effectively y-symmetrised when loaded with it on; bc.consistency_* refit checkpoints are trained to behave the same either way. Cost: the policy is discontinuous across y = 0 wherever the underlying network is asymmetric.
ppo._comment_log_flip_consistency: Log-only. When true (and augment_n_slot_shuffles > 0), every [PPO] block gets a `flip` line: the analytic KL between the policy on each rollout state and the y-mirror of the policy on its flip_y-augmented copy (summed over heads, the same quantity bc.consistency_* trains down), the move_dir angle error between the two, and the hard-decision disagreement rates of the exec Bernoulli heads. Computed from the pass _ppo_update already makes over the augmented batch (pre-update weights), so it costs one extra KL computation over the base rows plus ~100 MB. Use it to see whether flip consistency degrades during PPO.
ppo._comment_gamma: Discount factor: how much future rewards are worth vs immediate ones. Think of it as 'I care about a reward in N steps at gamma^N of its face value'. Standard range in the literature is roughly 0.95–0.999, with 0.99 a common default. Longer episodes / sparser terminal rewards generally favour values nearer the top of that range; short, densely-rewarded episodes can use a lower value without losing much signal. Raise it if the agent seems short-sighted about distant rewards; lower it if training variance looks too high.
ppo._comment_lam: GAE lambda: controls the bias/variance tradeoff in advantage estimation. lam=1.0 is pure Monte Carlo (low bias, high variance — noisy but unbiased). lam=0.0 is pure TD(0) (high bias, low variance — smooth but wrong). Standard range is roughly 0.9–0.99, with 0.95 a common default. Lower it if gradients are noisy and training oscillates; raise it if advantage estimates look too biased/smoothed.
ppo._comment_clip_range: PPO clipping: the policy ratio (new_prob / old_prob) is clamped to [1-clip, 1+clip]. This stops a single update from changing the policy too drastically — the gradient is zeroed for any sample where the ratio goes outside the band. Standard range is roughly 0.1–0.3, with 0.2 the most common default. Lower = more conservative updates (fewer minibatches survive the clip, more stable); raise it if updates feel too constrained or too few minibatches get through per rollout. Works together with target_kl below as the actual trust-region constraint.
ppo._comment_vf_coef: Value function loss coefficient: scales how hard the critic trains relative to the actor. total_loss = policy_loss + vf_coef*value_loss - ent_coef*entropy. Typical literature default: 0.5 (inherited from the original PPO/A2C-era benchmarks, tuned on much simpler single-head action spaces than this network's -- not derived for a multi-head policy sharing a trunk with a ret_var-normalized value loss). Raised to 2.0 for run 307b (from 0.5) after a direct measurement (isolated backward() on policy_loss alone vs vf_coef*value_loss alone, execution_net.trunk grad norm) found policy's shared-trunk gradient consistently ~10-18x larger than value's across 3 checkpoints -- a candidate explanation for why PPG-refit value quality (val_pre pushed to ~0.075-0.08) erodes back to ~0.095-0.1 within a handful of live-PPO checkpoints (see ai/knowledge.md and memory). 2.0 (4x) only delayed the climb by ~1 checkpoint before val_pre returned to the same ~0.10 plateau -- didn't change the equilibrium. Raised to 4.0 (8x, run 307c) as a bigger step, still short of full gradient-norm parity (~8x-18x depending on checkpoint) -- ALSO never shifted the plateau (held through run 307c/307d/308, ~250+ checkpoints). ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-09-23, not vf_coef at all): episode replay (`episode_replay_enabled`, top `episode_replay_top_fraction`=20% of each rollout's episodes by |advantage| re-queued for the NEXT rollout only) means every fresh process's first live-PPO rollout is 'clean' (`_pending_replay_before` inits empty, in-memory only, never saved to the checkpoint) while every rollout from the second onward carries a 20% replay batch of the hardest-to-predict episodes -- a genuine, permanent, ONE-TIME step change in dataset composition timed exactly at checkpoint1->checkpoint2 of every restart, not a gradient-training-speed problem vf_coef could ever fix. Explains why raising vf_coef never moved the plateau: the value function wasn't undertrained, the data genuinely got harder starting checkpoint 2 and stayed there. Cut back to 2.0 for run 309 -- the original gradient-imbalance finding (10-18x at 0.5) is still real and still worth the 2.0 correction, just not worth chasing further since 4.0's ADDITIONAL push over 2.0 was answering a question (fix the plateau) that turned out not to be a vf_coef question at all. Not rigorously confirmed by a controlled A/B (e.g. episode_replay_enabled=false for one comparison run) -- the timing match (jump lands exactly when replay first activates, then roughly holds rather than continuing to climb) is suggestive, not proof; redo that comparison if this explanation ever needs firmer footing.
ppo._comment_ent_coef: Legacy constant entropy coefficient -- only used as the DEFAULT for ent_coef_start below when that key is absent. total_loss = policy_loss + vf_coef*value_loss - ent_coef*entropy, so this is a FIXED per-step reward for being uncertain, with no self-limiting mechanism: the policy-gradient term's opposing pull shrinks as advantages shrink over training, but a constant ent_coef's pull does not, so entropy can win by default late in training even at a small value. Typical values are small, roughly 0.0-0.02. Prefer annealing via ent_coef_start/end/anneal_fraction below instead of relying on this constant, and watch per-head entropy in the training log for unbounded growth.
ppo._comment_ent_coef_anneal: Linear anneal of the entropy coefficient from ent_coef_start to ent_coef_end, reaching ent_coef_end by ent_coef_anneal_fraction of total_steps and holding flat after (same shape as bc.aux_coeff_start/end/anneal_fraction). Defaults to a no-op (constant at ent_coef_start, itself defaulting to the legacy ent_coef above) when these three keys are absent, so existing configs/checkpoints are unaffected until set explicitly. A common pattern is to anneal toward a small nonzero floor rather than exactly 0, so some exploration persists throughout training. Use the per-rollout '[per-head entropy]' log line and the 'value' line's |adv| figure to check whether entropy is still rising / whether |adv| has bottomed out, and adjust the endpoint accordingly.
ppo._comment_max_grad_norm: Gradient clipping: if the total gradient vector has magnitude > this, all gradients are scaled down proportionally. Acts as a safety valve against catastrophic updates from rare high-loss samples. 0.5 is standard for PPO. Raise to 1.0 if gradients feel too constrained (loss barely moves per step); lower to 0.3 if you see sudden policy collapses. Check the 'g=' value in the per-rollout log — if it's consistently hitting 0.5 exactly, you're clipping every update. Does NOT apply to the direction-head params (move_direction/kick_direction weights + move_dir_log_kappa/kick_dir_log_kappa/kick_dir_z_log_std) when direction_max_grad_norm below is set — those get their own isolated clip_grad_norm_() call.
ppo._comment_direction_max_grad_norm: Optional separate gradient-norm clip applied ONLY to the direction-head params (move_direction/kick_direction Linear weights + move_dir_log_kappa/kick_dir_log_kappa/kick_dir_z_log_std). null (default) = fall back to max_grad_norm, i.e. direction params are clipped together with everything else in one combined-norm group (prior behaviour). Set a float to isolate direction gradients into their own clip so a single outlier sample's large move_dir/kick_dir gradient can no longer force a proportional shrink of the rest of the network's gradient in the same step (and vice versa — a calm direction gradient no longer 'borrows' clip headroom from a genuinely large gradient elsewhere). There's no universal standard value for this kind of isolated per-group clip — start well under the main max_grad_norm and watch the '[grad clip] direction: N/M steps clipped (%) pre-clip norm mean=X max=Y' log line: raise if it's clipping most steps at a max far above the limit (signal still being choked), lower if it rarely engages and direction KL/ratio outliers appear.
ppo._comment_learning_rate: Step size for the policy's Adam optimiser. From-scratch PPO commonly uses roughly 1e-4 to 3e-4. When continuing from a BC-pretrained policy (as here), a much smaller LR is typical — often 1e-6 to 1e-5 — since large steps risk undoing an already-good policy, and augmentation (augment_n_slot_shuffles) effectively multiplies the batch size, further increasing each step's signal. Raise if training feels too slow; lower if the policy degrades/collapses after pretraining. Does NOT apply to the direction-head params when direction_learning_rate below is set — those get their own Adam param group/LR.
ppo._comment_direction_learning_rate: Optional separate Adam LR for the direction-head param group (move_direction/kick_direction weights + move_dir_log_kappa/kick_dir_log_kappa/kick_dir_z_log_std). null (default) = fall back to learning_rate, i.e. direction params share the main 'policy' param group's LR (prior behaviour). Set a float smaller than learning_rate to directly shrink how much move_direction's predicted mean can move per gradient step, independent of the rest of the policy — complementary to direction_max_grad_norm (LR scales the step size AFTER grad-norm clipping bounds the raw gradient magnitude).
ppo._comment_value_learning_rate: Separate LR for the value_head (+ value_extra_mlp) param group only, typically set higher than the (often deliberately tiny, see learning_rate above) policy LR — sharing one LR with the critic tends to starve value learning, especially since the per-minibatch KL early-stop (see target_kl) is based on policy KL alone and can cut a rollout's gradient steps short regardless of how well the value function is tracking returns. Comparable in scale to value_pretrain_lr/demo_value_pretrain_lr. Falls back to `learning_rate` if absent.
ppo._comment_value_weight_decay: Adam weight_decay (L2) applied ONLY to the value param group ('value_head'/'value_ai_type_channel' params, or trainer.value_net's optimizer when --separate-value-net) during PPO. 0.0 (default) = disabled, matching prior behaviour. Each rollout's data is used for only ppo.n_epochs passes and the return distribution keeps shifting under self-play, so overfitting-to-one-batch is less of a risk here than in bc.value_pretrain_weight_decay's offline setting -- this is mainly cheap insurance for generalisation across the whole run. Try 1e-4 to 1e-3.
ppo._comment_value_only_continuation_epochs: Epoch budget for the value-only continuation loop that runs after the policy's per-minibatch KL early-stop cuts the main epoch loop short (see target_kl) — trains ONLY the value_head/value_extra_mlp param group (no policy forward/backward, so no further KL risk) for up to this many additional passes over the same rollout batch. Defaults to n_epochs if absent (previous, implicit behaviour was to reuse n_epochs unconditionally). Raise if 'val=' stays high despite frequent early-stops; lower if you're worried about overfitting the critic to a single stale rollout batch (see ai/knowledge.md).
ppo._comment_target_kl: Per-minibatch early-stop threshold. KL divergence measures how much the policy distribution has changed since the rollout was collected — KL=0 means no change. When any minibatch's KL exceeds this, the entire epoch loop stops early. Standard values in most PPO implementations are small, roughly 0.01–0.05; a value much larger than that effectively disables this safety net (real per-minibatch KL rarely reaches it), leaving clip_range as the only real trust-region constraint. Lower this to make early-stop fire sooner and protect the policy more aggressively — fewer minibatches per rollout but more stable training. Raise it to let more of the rollout's gradient budget be used per update.
ppo._comment_n_processes: Number of worker PROCESSES for the MAIN PPO training loop's on-policy rollout collection ONLY -- pretrain_value()/pretrain_combined()'s separate value-warm-up rollout uses its own value_pretrain_n_processes below instead (deliberately decoupled, see that key's comment). 1 (default) = single-process behaviour, no subprocess overhead. >1 spawns that many subprocesses (see ai/ppo/rollout_worker.py, or ai/ppo/batched_rollout_worker.py when batched_rollout is true below), each with its own env + local policy copy, weight-synced from the main process before every rollout -- see ai_trainer_knowledge.md 'Parallel rollout collection'. Physics stepping is pure-Python/CPU-bound (GIL-limited under threads), so this only helps via real OS processes. Does NOT affect BC pre-training's dataset epochs or the PPO/value gradient updates themselves -- those stay single-process. n_processes is ALWAYS literally the process count, whether or not batched_rollout is on -- total envs = n_processes * envs_per_process (envs_per_process defaults to 1 when batched_rollout is false, so n_processes alone is total envs too in that case). No divisibility constraint between the two: unlike an earlier design where a single 'total envs' knob had to be an exact multiple of envs_per_process, n_processes and envs_per_process are independent, which is exactly why they're two separate keys instead of one.
ppo._comment_batched_rollout: When true, the MAIN PPO loop's rollout collection uses ai/ppo/batched_rollout_worker.py instead of rollout_worker.py: each of n_processes worker processes owns envs_per_process ScenarioEnv instances and batches ALL of their trainee decisions into ONE PPOTrainer._sample_action_batch() network call per round, instead of each process doing its own batch-of-1 call. False (default) = today's one-env-per-process behaviour via rollout_worker.py (envs_per_process ignored). Has NO effect on pretrain_value()/pretrain_combined()'s separate value-warm-up rollout collection (see value_pretrain_n_processes) -- that path has no batched-rollout-aware implementation yet. Benchmarked this session (10800-step rollouts, this machine's 6 physical cores): with the per-row sampling tail also vectorized (_sample_action_from_heads_batch), 3 processes x 10 envs_per_process (30 total envs) measured 2.17x the throughput of a 6-process/1-env-each baseline -- and the win kept growing with envs_per_process (3x3=1.29x, 3x4=1.58x, 5x5=1.98x, 3x10=2.17x) with no plateau found yet, so envs_per_process is the lever to raise further if you want to keep pushing this, not n_processes alone. Plain one-env-per-process oversubscription past ~2x physical cores gets WORSE, not better (25 procs measured 0.66x, 30 procs even crashed one benchmark run via a memory-pressure spike during process teardown/spawn overlap) -- batching is what lets total env count keep climbing without that collapse. Re-benchmark if the model/batch size/hardware changes materially; there's no universal best value.
ppo._comment_envs_per_process: Envs per worker process when batched_rollout is true (ignored otherwise, where it's implicitly 1). Total envs = n_processes * envs_per_process; n_processes above is always the literal process count, independent of this value -- no divisibility constraint between them. Raising this increases the batch size of each round's ONE decision-network call (more amortization of Python/PyTorch dispatch overhead per row) while holding process count down -- see _comment_batched_rollout for the benchmark data motivating the current value.
ppo._comment_batch_secondary_players: Only meaningful alongside batched_rollout=true. When true, ALSO batches every secondary/opponent neural player's decision (e.g. phase 1's self-play 'neural remainder' opponent -- see curriculum.phase1_opponent_neural_ratio, often the majority of episodes) into its own one-call-per-round batch, using the SAME trainer as the primary (true self-play, identical weights, just batched). False (default) = secondary players decide unbatched, one at a time, via their own sample_action_fn fallback -- only the trainee's decision is batched. See ai/ppo/batched_rollout_worker.py's module docstring.
ppo._comment_episode_replay: Only meaningful alongside batched_rollout=true. When episode_replay_enabled is true, at the end of each rollout the top episode_replay_top_fraction of that rollout's episodes (by mean(|advantage|), the same per-episode metric the '[advantage |.| by episode]' log line reports) have their exact scenario SEED re-queued for the VERY NEXT rollout only -- a Prioritized-Level-Replay-style re-exposure to whatever the policy found most surprising/informative, one-shot (not an ongoing replay buffer: a queued seed not consumed next rollout, because no env happened to reset while it was queued, is simply dropped rather than carried further). A '[episode replay]' log line reports before-vs-after mean reward for whichever queued seeds actually got replayed. Raised from 0.2 to 0.25 on 2026-09-23 (run 309b evidence: replayed episodes showed a large, real reward improvement the second time through -- e.g. mean -0.02 -> +0.17 in one observed cycle -- suggesting the mechanism is working well enough to lean into slightly harder; not escalated further without more evidence). Like every other __init__-time config value, this is read once when the trainer is constructed, so the bump only takes effect on the NEXT fresh `train.py` launch -- it does nothing to a process already running. False (default) = no effect: every episode reset draws a fresh random seed exactly as before this feature existed (seeds are still recorded internally either way, just never re-queued). See ai/ppo/batched_rollout_worker.py's 'Episode-seed replay' docstring section and PPOTrainer._update_episode_replay().
ppo._comment_value_pretrain_n_processes: Worker-process count for pretrain_value()'s own rollout collection (also used by pretrain_combined()'s Phase 2/3 value warm-up) -- a SEPARATE setting from n_processes above, on purpose. This path (_collect_value_pretrain_rollout) spawns plain one-env-per-process rollout_worker.py workers by default, or batched_rollout_worker.py workers when value_pretrain_batched_rollout is true (see below) -- either way it is deliberately decoupled from the main loop's n_processes, since sharing it directly would silently inherit whatever (likely much larger, batching-oriented) process count the main PPO loop uses, and per this session's benchmarking naive one-env-per-process oversubscription well past physical core count makes throughput WORSE, not better (see _comment_batched_rollout). 9 is a modest, known-safe process count for the plain (unbatched) mode on a ~6-physical-core machine; raise only alongside actual core count.
ppo._comment_value_pretrain_batched_rollout: When true, pretrain_value()/pretrain_combined()'s value-warm-up rollout AND ppg_value_refit()'s rollout use ai/ppo/batched_rollout_worker.py (each of value_pretrain_n_processes processes owns value_pretrain_envs_per_process envs and batches ALL their decisions into one network call per round -- the same mechanism the main PPO loop uses, see _comment_batched_rollout for its measured 2x+ throughput win) instead of plain one-env-per-process workers that do a batch-of-1 network call per env per step. Total envs = value_pretrain_n_processes * value_pretrain_envs_per_process. batch_secondary_players (main-loop setting above) is reused, so self-play opponents are batched too. Not chunk-streamed on purpose: the value-pretrain path needs whole episodes (MC returns, a clean train/val episode split), and with ~50-step episodes a chunk boundary would split a large fraction of them -- memory profile is therefore the same as the plain path (one result per worker at the end). false (default, opt-in) = today's plain workers, unchanged.
ppo._comment_value_pretrain_envs_per_process: Envs per worker process when value_pretrain_batched_rollout is true (ignored otherwise). Independent of ppo.envs_per_process (same reason value_pretrain_n_processes is independent of ppo.n_processes). Raising it increases the batch size of each round's ONE decision-network call while holding process count down; the main loop's live 17 x 12 is a reasonable starting point.
ppo._comment_worker_torch_threads: torch.set_num_threads() inside each rollout worker process (see n_processes). Each worker only ever does batch-of-1 CPU forward passes, so >1 thread just adds intra-process contention across N worker processes competing for the same cores; 1 (default) is correct almost always.
ppo._comment_main_process_torch_threads: torch.set_num_threads() in the main process for train.py and debug_value_network.py -- BC pre-training and the PPO/value gradient update run small-batch ops here, unrelated to worker_torch_threads/n_processes above. Unlike batch-of-1 rollout workers, letting PyTorch default to all cores can measurably slow small-batch ops down (thread-sync overhead per op can exceed the compute saved), so a capped value is often faster than either 1 or os.cpu_count() in practice. Worth re-benchmarking on your own hardware if the model or batch size changes materially -- there's no single universal best value.
ppo._comment_dir_log_kappa_headroom: dir_log_kappa_min/max bound how small/large the move-direction von Mises log_kappa can grow (log_kappa is the actual optimised parameter; the clamp zeroes gradient once it drifts past a bound). NOTE the inverted relationship vs the old log_std: larger log_kappa = MORE concentrated (narrower), so 'headroom to widen' now means headroom toward log_kappa_min, not max. A smaller kappa also directly shrinks the von Mises KL term for a given amount of angular drift in the predicted mean, which matters for target_kl-based early-stopping -- same qualitative effect as widening sigma did before, just via the opposite end of the parameter's range.
ppo._comment_dir_log_kappa_reg: Explicit L2 restoring force pulling move_dir_log_kappa toward dir_log_kappa_target and kick_dir_log_kappa toward kick_dir_log_kappa_target (and kick_dir_z_log_std toward kick_dir_z_log_std_target, same mechanism as the old log_std reg). move_* keys fall back to dir_log_kappa_*/dir_log_std_* for backward compat. Without this, the direction heads' entropy bonus only ever pulls log_kappa toward LOWER (wider) values with nothing pulling it back up. 0.0 = disabled. Try 0.01-0.1.
ppo._comment_kick_power_spin_log_std_init: Initial log_std for the kick_power (SquashedNormalHead, sigmoid-squashed scalar in [0,1]) and kick_spin (plain unsquashed 3D Normal -- kick_spin has no bounded physical range wired up yet, still disabled at the apply_nn_action.py chokepoint per agent_plans/spin_implementation_plan.md) heads. 0.0 preserves the original nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(...)) init, i.e. moderate exploration noise around the predicted mean from the start. Lower (more negative) for less initial exploration noise on these heads; raise for more.
ppo._comment_ent_kick_power_spin_weight: Entropy bonus weight for the kick_power (SquashedNormalHead) and kick_spin (plain 3D Normal) heads, both E[kick active]-weighted -- matching how sprint/move_dir/kick_dir are weighted by their own parent-active probability in _compute_entropy. Separate weight from move_dir/kick_dir's (ent_move_dir_weight / ent_kick_weight+ent_kick_dir_azimuth_only_weight+ent_kick_dir_z_only_weight) since neither kick_power nor kick_spin is a DirectionHead (unit-vector Gaussian).
ppo._comment_ent_decision_weight: Weight applied to decision_net's own 7 Bernoulli heads (shoot, pass, move, tackle, get_possession_raw, mark, hold_position) in the entropy bonus ONLY (_compute_entropy) -- separate from execution_net's exec_move/sprint/kick/tackle_attempt Bernoullis, which always keep weight 1.0 regardless of this key. A head currently frozen for the curriculum phase (see PPOTrainer.set_frozen_heads()) already contributes exactly zero here regardless of this weight, so in practice this only affects whichever decision heads are currently unfrozen. 0.0 disables entropy-driven exploration pressure for those heads entirely — appropriate once you want them to converge confidently toward a fixed behaviour (e.g. 'always attempt') rather than keep exploring; raise back toward 1.0 once a later phase needs them to explore alternatives again.
ppo._comment_augment: Slot permutations per geometric flip variant. Total batch multiplier = N_FLIP_VARIANTS(2) * n. Use 1 for 2x (flip_y only), 3 for 6x, 0 to disable. flip_x is no longer part of this random augmentation -- it's now a permanent canonical-AI-frame transform, see ai/obs/canonical.py. See ai/obs/augment.py.
ppo._comment_rollout_eval: Number of trials run vs rules-based AI after each PPO rollout update. Set to 0 to disable the per-rollout eval entirely.
ppo._comment: Standard PPO defaults from CleanRL-style reference implementations. Tune empirically.
ppo._comment_ent_coef_run305: Re-based at restart for run 305 (continues run 304's schedule): run 304 started at step 451,407,647 with total-steps 200,000,000, ent_coef 0.005 -> 0.001 over 0.6 of that, i.e. reaching 0.001 at step 571,407,647. Run 305 restarts at step 545,964,837 with --total-steps 105,500,000, so progress restarts at 0: ent_coef_start is run 304's value at the restart step and the anneal fraction is set so it still reaches 0.001 at the same absolute step. progress only drives ent_coef (learning_rate/clip_range are constant, bc coefficients are 0).
ppo._comment_ent_coef_run306: Run 305 finished with ent_coef already flat at its 0.001 floor for its whole back half (reached ~step 572-576M). Run 306 continues from run 305's final checkpoint142 (step 651,779,260) -- since progress restarts at 0 on every new train.py invocation, leaving ent_coef_start at run 305's re-based value (0.0018481) would have jumped ent_coef straight back UP at the start of run 306, undoing the anneal. Set flat at 0.001 (start=end=1.0 frac) instead: no more annealing needed, it was already at the floor.
ppo._comment_ent_coef_run308: Doubled the flat floor 0.001 -> 0.002 for run 308, on the observation that most heads looked like they needed more exploration pressure, e.g. exec_move/sprint/tackle_attempt have no dedicated per-head multiplier and were riding on the base coefficient alone -- these now get roughly 2x their old entropy pressure automatically. The GENERIC per-head base multipliers (ent_kick_power_weight, ent_kick_spin_weight) were left at a flat 1.0 (not halved to fully offset the base doubling -- these heads get somewhat more net pressure than before too, deliberately, same reasoning as the unweighted heads). ent_dir_weight (the equivalent shared base multiplier for move_dir/kick_dir, also 1.0) was removed from the codebase entirely right after this rebalance -- it was pure overhead by then (move_dir and kick_dir already have fully independent dedicated multipliers below, and ent_dir_weight had never actually been used to scale them as a group), so at 1.0 removing it changed nothing. ent_move_dir_weight/ent_kick_weight were cut roughly proportionally (10->5.5, 6->3.5, using 1+(weight-1)/2 for the additive-boost ones -- see _compute_entropy) since move_dir's sharpening is already tamed and didn't need extra pressure. ent_kick_power_only_weight and ent_kick_dir_only_weight were deliberately left UNCUT (still 24.0/15.0) despite the base doubling -- these are the actively-fought kick_power/kick_dir sharpening levers (see their own comments) and the base bump is meant to ADD to their effect, not be absorbed by a compensating cut, especially right after this run's kick_power/kick_dir value+Adam resets.
ppo._comment_move_dir_log_kappa_max: Hard cap on the move_dir von Mises log-concentration (forward() clamps to it): kappa <= 1000. Falls back to dir_log_kappa_max when unset, so kick_dir keeps 10.0. Added because the move_dir head's gradient norm grew ~ kappa^0.4 over run 304 and the main-group grad clip reached ~50% of steps.
ppo._comment_ent_move_dir_weight: Extra multiplier on the move_dir entropy bonus in the PPO loss ONLY (on top of the ent_coef schedule); 1.0 = old behaviour exactly. Carried in the same separate term as ent_kick_weight so the logged entropy and per-head breakdown stay unboosted, and P(exec_move) is detached so the boost reaches only move_dir_log_kappa (the von Mises entropy depends on kappa alone), pulling it down = slower sharpening, without also pushing the exec_move gate toward standing still. Added for run 305 (weight 8.0) because move_dir kappa kept sharpening (about +0.011 in log kappa per checkpoint through run 304) and its gradient norm grew ~kappa^0.4. Run 305 showed weight 8 roughly HALVES the drift rather than stopping it (kappa still climbed 128 -> 266 over the run, log-kappa drift ~+0.0055-0.0063/checkpoint at the ent_coef floor, vs run 304's unweighted ~+0.011-0.013/checkpoint) and the main-group grad-clip share was already back up to 8-13% by the end (was 1-2% right after the reset) -- run 304's clip share coincided with a vs-rules eval plateau once it passed roughly 13-22% (peaked ~log60/kappa229/clip13%, then flat through 50% clip), so run 306 raised the weight to 10.0 to push a bit harder against the regrowth. By the end of run 306, move_dir kappa growth was essentially flat (+0.00056 log-kappa/checkpoint over the whole run) -- weight 10 worked for this head. Lowered to 5.5 for run 308 as part of a GLOBAL rebalance (see _comment_ent_coef_run308), not because move_dir itself regressed: ent_coef_start/end doubled 0.001->0.002 and every per-head multiplier was cut to hold each already-tuned head's NET pressure roughly constant (move_dir's boost term is additive as (weight-1)*..., so the compensating value is 1+(10-1)/2=5.5, not 10/2) while heads with no dedicated multiplier get the full 2x from the base bump. Lowered again 5.5 -> 4.0 for run 311 for the identical reason (ent_coef 0.002 -> 0.003, 1.5x, same compensating formula) -- see _comment_ent_coef_20260924; move_dir itself was still behaving fine at the end of run 310 (steady kappa growth, no collapse), this is purely a rebalance, not a response to a move_dir-specific problem.
ppo._comment_ent_kick_power_only_weight: Same idea as ent_move_dir_weight but for kick_power_log_std specifically. Unlike ent_kick_weight (which deliberately ALSO pushes p(kick) itself, added to stop the kick gate collapsing early -- see its comment), this detaches the kick-gate's contribution to kick_power's (E[kick]-weighted) entropy term, so the boost reaches ONLY kick_power_log_std, never kick_logit -- same detach-the-gate pattern as ent_move_dir_weight, see _compute_entropy. Added for run 307: with move_dir's growth tamed by weight 10, the SAME main-group-grad-clip mechanism (a head's spread param sharpening, backpropagating through the shared trunk, inflating the shared clip-group norm and collaterally shrinking every other head's gradient) shifted to kick_power instead -- it was NOT in run 305/306's problem list because move_dir dominated, but by run 306's end its sigma had roughly halved (0.34 -> 0.17 over that run alone) with its per-head KL still ACCELERATING (0.0098 -> 0.0365, not levelling off) and entropy crossed from positive to negative (sigma small enough that a Gaussian's differential entropy goes negative). kick_power_log_std is NOT in the isolated direction_max_grad_norm clip group (that's only move_direction/kick_direction weights + move_dir_log_kappa/kick_dir_log_kappa/kick_dir_z_log_std), so its gradient was inflating the shared 'main' group's norm exactly like move_dir's did in run 304 -- main-group clip climbed 6% -> 19% over run 306 even as move_dir's own contribution had gone flat. 8.0 (run 307's first guess, same order as move_dir's initial pick) measurably FAILED: over runs 307/307b/307c (~250 checkpoints after the sigma reset to 0.4), log_std drift was -0.0069/checkpoint, if anything SLIGHTLY FASTER than run 306's unweighted -0.0062/checkpoint -- essentially zero protective effect, unlike move_dir where the same weight (8) at least halved the drift. Raised to 24.0 (3x) for run 307d, alongside dropping kick_power_log_std's Adam optimizer state (see kick_power_kick_dir_adam_reset.py in the scratchpad) on the theory that its accumulated per-parameter Adam moment history, built almost entirely under one-directional 'get sharper' reward pressure before this weight existed, may have been dampening the entropy term's effective pull regardless of nominal coefficient size (same lead hypothesis as the vf_coef investigation, see project_vf_coef_grad_probe_findings memory) -- watch whether the FRESH Adam state lets a big weight actually gain traction this time, not just whether 24 alone does more than 8 did. RESULT: weight 24 + Adam reset worked for the first ~3 checkpoints (log_std drift ~-0.0024/checkpoint, roughly half the old unweighted rate) but then faded -- by checkpoint4-6 the drift had stepped back up to ~-0.0050 to -0.0066/checkpoint, essentially back to the unweighted baseline, with per-head KL climbing again too. The slowdown was real but transient, not a fix. For run 308: alongside the base ent_coef doubling (see _comment_ent_coef_run308), this weight was deliberately left UNCUT at 24.0 (unlike most other multipliers) so the doubled base ADDS to its effect rather than being offset by a compensating cut -- also hard-reset kick_power_log_std itself from run307d checkpoint6's 0.1614 to 0.25 (a 'little less sharp', not all the way back to the earlier 0.4 reset) plus a fresh Adam state again (kick_power_kickdir_value_reset.py), then ran 5 rounds of PPG value refit on the reset checkpoint before resuming live PPO -- watch whether combining a real value reset with stronger, not just rebalanced, entropy pressure holds up longer than the Adam-reset-alone attempt did. ppo._comment_ent_kick_dir_azimuth_only_weigh: Same pattern as ent_kick_power_only_weight, for kick_dir_log_kappa (the azimuthal/in-plane component of kick_dir) specifically. bc._comment_ppg_lr_20260923: Cut 5e-5 -> 3e-5 alongside the main PPO learning_rate/direction_learning_rate/value_learning_rate cut (see that comment near the top of the ppo section) for the run309b -> run310 restart, to keep the PPG refit's LR scale matched to the main loop's.
bc._comment_ppg_warmup_steps: Raised from 50 to 120 on 2026-09-23. The epoch-by-epoch kl_train pattern (both run309b interleave rounds tonight) is remarkably consistent: low at epoch 1, PEAKS at epoch 2 (~0.015-0.016), then settles back down through epochs 3-6. With minibatch_size=12000 against a ~770k-step rollout (~64 minibatches/epoch), the old 50-step warmup fully ramped to full LR within epoch 1 alone -- by epoch 2 warmup had already completely expired, giving that epoch zero protection, which lines up exactly with the peak landing there every time. This contradicts the older claim in _comment_lr_warmup_steps that '25-50 steps removed its early-KL bump' -- that claim is now suspect (either it was about a narrower single-minibatch spike, not this epoch-level pattern, or it never held up under real interleave testing) and should be treated as unverified until re-checked. 120 steps spans roughly epochs 1-2, so epoch 2 should now get partial warmup protection too -- watch whether the peak shrinks or just shifts to epoch 3 (i.e. whether this fixes the mechanism or just delays it), which would point back toward ppg_kl_coef or something else being the real driver despite the earlier negative result there.
bc._comment_ppg_interleave: Run bursts of ppg_value_refit() mid-PPO (see PPOTrainer._maybe_run_ppg_interleave, checked once per rollout at the same point as the neural-snapshot eval) instead of only via the standalone --ppg-refit-only entry point, so a refit no longer requires stopping and restarting the process. Reuses ppg_value_refit() completely unchanged -- this is only a trigger, not a new refit implementation. false (default) disables the check entirely, byte-identical to before this existed. Two ways to fire once enabled, checked in this order and not mutually exclusive: (1) manual -- touch (create) the file ppg_interleave_trigger_file points at (or '<checkpoint_dir>/ppg_trigger' if that key is null) at any time while the run is live; it's deleted the moment it's noticed, so one touch fires exactly one burst, and this is the primary intended use ('whenever we need it we get some rounds of PPG'), not an automatic plateau-detection heuristic (none of those were judged reliable enough to build -- every PPG call this project has made so far was a human judgment call, e.g. 'we just reset kick_power's sigma, let's refit now'). (2) cadence safety net -- ppg_interleave_cadence_rollouts > 0 also fires automatically every N rollouts (counted since the last interleave fired, manual or cadence), 0 = off. ppg_interleave_num_rollouts/ppg_interleave_n_steps set the burst's own num_rollouts/n_steps (independent of ppg_num_rollouts/ppg_rollout_steps above, which are for the standalone --ppg-refit-only path -- keep them smaller here since a live run pays for this burst out of the SAME wall-clock budget as normal training, unlike the standalone path). The burst spawns its own worker pool sequentially with the main loop's (never concurrently -- we're only ever called between one rollout's update and the next one's collection), and an extra checkpoint is saved right after the burst so its effect isn't lost if the process dies before the next natural checkpoint. See project_ppg_interleave_design memory for why this reuses ppg_value_refit() as-is (the 'easy version') rather than sharing the main loop's already-spawned workers (a bigger, riskier change, not done).
bc._comment_ppg_rollout_deterministic: EXPERIMENT (leave false for real use). When true, ppg_value_refit's rollouts are collected with the policy acting deterministically (each head's mode/mean, no sampling -- both sides of self-play, since the opponent is the same network) instead of sampling, to test how much of the value-loss floor is the agent's own action-sampling noise: if the per-rollout loss drops sharply and the paired compare starts showing gains, that noise is the floor. Caveats: the value head then learns V of the DETERMINISTIC policy (a different quantity from the stochastic policy's V that PPO uses), so don't keep a checkpoint refit this way for training without thinking; and '[ppg compare]' scores the (stochastically-trained) original on deterministic data, so a positive delta there partly just reflects that shift. Needs ppo.value_pretrain_batched_rollout=true. An env that is not due for a decision that round (rare early-exit) still samples via its own fallback.
bc._comment_ppg_seed_adam_variance: EXPERIMENT, added 2026-09-23, untested (leave false until deliberately tried on its own, isolated from other config changes). When true, ppg_value_refit's fresh throwaway Adam optimizer has each parameter's exp_avg_sq (Adam's per-parameter variance/step-size estimate) AND step count seeded from the LIVE ppo.optimizer's current state before the refit starts, instead of starting fully cold (all zeros). Momentum (exp_avg) is explicitly zeroed regardless -- only the variance-based step-size calibration is borrowed, never the live optimizer's actual gradient-direction momentum, since that points toward PPO's clipped-surrogate objective, not this refit's value-loss+KL-anchor one. Strictly one-directional and read-only (cloned tensors copied INTO the fresh optimizer; ppo.optimizer itself is never written to), so this can never affect the live PPO optimizer regardless of how the refit goes -- see the seeding block right after ppg_opt's construction in ppg_value_refit() for the mechanism, including why the step count has to travel with exp_avg_sq (Adam's bias-correction denominator assumes exp_avg_sq grew from zero over that many steps; seeding a mature exp_avg_sq at step=0 would badly over-correct). Motivation: [[project_kick_power_ppg_kl_investigation]] -- move_dir's kappa disproportionately dominates PPG-refit KL, tripling ppg_kl_coef didn't fix it, and Adam's own per-parameter step-size normalization (cold-started every refit call) was the untested lead hypothesis. Deliberately kept OUT of the run309b->run310 restart (2026-09-23) that changed learning_rate/direction_learning_rate/value_learning_rate/ppg_lr (5e-5->3e-5) at the same time, so any change in the epoch-2 KL peak shape can still be attributed to a single cause -- test this as its own isolated interleave round once run310 is stable, not bundled with the LR change.
bc._comment_ppg_loss_diagnostics: Log-only. On cycle 1 and every ppg_diag_every_n_cycles-th cycle, ppg_value_refit logs a breakdown of where the value error lives, on that rollout's fresh rows before training on them (identity copies only, finished-episode rows only, against pure-MC returns): by episode outcome, by row owner (trainee/opponent track) vs the other player's AI type (rules/immobile/neural), by position within the episode (quartiles), error concentration (share of total squared error from the worst 1%/10% of rows), the within-outcome vs between-outcome variance decomposition (how much of the error is just predicting the outcome), a decile calibration table (predicted value -> realised return) and the 5 worst rows; with ppg_compare_to_original also the original net's MSE per group. Also saves the per-row arrays (mc, gae_return, preds, phase, dones, other_ai_type, track, outcome) to <checkpoint_dir>/ppg_diag_cycle<k>.npz for offline slicing (~15-30 MB each). Costs 1-2 extra forward passes over the rollout's rows on printing cycles.
bc._comment_ppg_compare_to_original: Log-only diagnostic for ppg_value_refit. Keeps a frozen copy of the decision/execution nets as loaded at the START of the call and, on every rollout's fresh rows (before training on them), scores both it and the current weights against PURE Monte-Carlo returns, logging '[ppg compare vs pure-MC returns] original=.. current=.. delta(original-current)=..' (positive = the refit is genuinely better). The paired difference cancels the rollout-to-rollout noise that makes the raw per-rollout baseline lines unreadable. MC targets on purpose, not GAE: GAE returns contain the SAMPLING network's own value predictions, so scoring any other network against them is biased toward the sampler by exactly their disagreement (which is the same size as the effect being measured). First cycle's delta is 0 by construction (same weights). Costs two extra forward passes over each rollout's train rows.
bc._comment_ppg_rmse_trim_frac: Log-only. ppg_value_refit's train/val lines additionally report 'rmse_exNN' / 'val_rmse_exNN': the RMSE after dropping the NN% (this fraction) of rows with the LARGEST squared error, so a small tail of badly mis-valued states doesn't hide whether the bulk of predictions is improving. Never affects training or early stopping (early stop still keys on plain val loss). 0 = the 'trimmed' figure equals the plain rmse.
bc._comment_consistency: flip_y consistency refit (train.py --consistency-refit-only; PPOTrainer.consistency_refit()). Opt-in: only runs when that flag is passed. Each of consistency_num_rollouts cycles collects consistency_rollout_steps steps with the CURRENT policy, then for every state uses the orientation where the observer's own y >= 0 as the primary one: a frozen teacher (the --checkpoint file, loaded WITHOUT any --reset-bernoullis/kappa reset) is evaluated on it and the student is trained (ppg-style analytic per-head KL) so the primary state gives the teacher's answer and its y-mirror gives the mirrored answer -- both orientations share one target, so the student becomes flip_y-consistent. consistency_logit_bound: Bernoulli TARGET logits are clamped to +-this (6.907 = probabilities within [0.001, 0.999]) so trained heads end up bounded; <=0 disables. consistency_kappa_deg: move_dir/kick_dir kappa is set to 1/radians(deg)^2 for the call (22 deg -> kappa 6.78); <=0 keeps the checkpoint kappa. Frozen for the call: all direction/power/spin spread params (a trainable kappa would let the consistency KL be lowered by just widening distributions), the value head + value-only modules (shared trunk still moves; value error is logged), physics encoders. Use --reset-bernoullis with --bernoulli-scale-<head> to flatten the four exec Bernoulli heads first so their gradients are not clamped away by the KL's +-12 logit clamp. consistency_lr/epochs/val_episode_fraction/warmup_steps mirror the ppg_* keys.
bc._comment: Behavioural cloning from rules-based AI. Set pretrain_steps=0 to skip pre-training. Set aux_coeff_start=0.0 to disable the PPO auxiliary BC loss.
bc._comment_direction_loss_mode: How the move_direction BC loss (bc_loss_from_tensor in bc.py) is computed. 'cosine' (default): 1 - cosine_similarity between the L2-normalized predicted direction and the target. This loss is scale-invariant in the raw (pre-normalize) output's magnitude, so nothing constrains that magnitude to stay well-conditioned, and the loss's own gradient w.r.t. the raw vector scales as 1/||raw|| -- can let ||raw|| drift over training while gradient norm shrinks in lockstep, a plausible source of outsized/spiky gradients on this head. 'mse': fit the raw pre-normalize vector directly via plain MSE against the (unit-length) target -- no division-by-norm anywhere in this loss's backward pass, so gradient magnitude is linear in the residual like ordinary regression; for two unit vectors, ||a-b||^2 == 2(1-cos(a,b)), so this converges to the SAME fixed point as 'cosine', just via better-conditioned gradients. PPO's own exploration (DirectionHead) needs no changes either way -- it already re-normalizes whatever raw vector it's given, defensively, regardless of this setting. direction_mag_reg_coef (see below) is INDEPENDENT of this setting -- applies regardless of mode.
bc._comment_direction_mag_reg_coef: Coefficient for an added (||raw|| - 1)^2 term on the PRE-normalize output of BOTH move_direction and kick_direction (same coefficient for both -- identical raw-Linear-then-L2-normalize architecture and issue). Computed by the standalone direction_magnitude_reg() (bc.py), applied UNCONDITIONALLY (independent of direction_loss_mode, independent of any BC label mask, independent of any other loss's own coefficient/anneal schedule) in every real training path that runs a backward pass through these heads: PPO's own policy-gradient update (_ppo_update's main loop), Phase 1 BC pretrain, BC-repair, PPO's bc-only continuation, and DAgger (dagger.py). A collapsing ||raw|| amplifies the L2-normalize op's gradient (roughly 1/||raw||), and nothing else in the PPO policy-gradient path constrains this once BC's own aux-loss coefficient anneals toward 0. 0.0 (default) = off, a true no-op. Try a small positive value (e.g. 0.01-0.1) if ||raw|| drifts far from 1 in training diagnostics.
bc._comment_label_smoothing: Label smoothing for BC Bernoulli targets before BCE: target = target*(1-eps) + 0.5*eps. dec_label_smoothing applies to the 7 decision heads (shoot/pass/move/tackle/gp_extra/mark/hold); exec_label_smoothing applies to the 4 execution Bernoulli heads (exec_move, sprint, kick_this_tick, tackle_attempt). 0.0 = disabled (default). Typical smoothing values are small, roughly 0.01-0.05 -- useful if BC-primed heads become overconfident and cause PPO's per-minibatch KL early-stop to fire immediately on the first rollout (very confident post-BC Bernoulli probabilities make Bernoulli KL highly nonlinear, so even a small first gradient step can overshoot target_kl).
bc._comment_pos_weight: null = auto-compute from the training dataset at load time via DemonstrationDataset.compute_pos_weights() (recommended). Set a float to override. pos_weight_max caps the auto-computed inverse-frequency ratio (e.g. tackle_attempt was hitting ~134.5) before use — null = uncapped. Only applies to the auto-computed path; has no effect when pos_weight_kick/pos_weight_tackle_attempt are set explicitly.
bc._comment_max_grad_norm: Grad-norm clip for BC pretrain's optimizers (Phase 0 demo_opt, Phase 1 bc_opt, Phase 4 repair_opt). Absent from config = fall back to ppo.max_grad_norm (prior behaviour, shares PPO's very conservative clip). Set a float here to give BC pretrain its own cap instead -- BC uses a much higher LR (bc_learning_rate) and full supervised minibatch descent with no PPO trust-region concept, so PPO's tight clip can suppress useful large early-training corrections. Set explicitly to null (as here) to disable clipping entirely during BC.
bc._comment_downsample: Gentle per-epoch downsampling of 'trivial' BC movement rows (see DemonstrationDataset._compute_trivial_mask). frac_default is used for epochs < epoch_threshold, frac_high_epoch afterward. Freshly re-rolled every epoch, never a fixed one-time filter. downsample_trivial_exclude_radius_steps also protects rows near a sprint/exec_move speedMode change, not just kick_this_tick/tackle_attempt.
bc._comment_aux: aux_coeff ('other'), kick_aux_coeff ('kick'), and tackle_aux_coeff ('tackle') each anneal linearly from their own start to end, sharing aux_coeff_anneal_fraction of training as the anneal duration (e.g. 0.3 = all three done by 30% of steps). Only used by the online BC-aux-during-PPO term in PPOTrainer._ppo_update() (Mode 3) -- the offline pretraining/repair BC passes in pretrain_combined() still use the single combined loss, unaffected by this split. The BC loss (bc_loss_from_tensor() in bc.py, split_kick=True, split_tackle=True) covers EVERYTHING: all 7 decision Bernoullis, move_region_center MSE, exec_move/sprint Bernoullis, and move_direction cosine are scaled by aux_coeff ('other' group); kick_this_tick Bernoulli, kick_direction cosine, kick_power MSE, and kick_spin MSE (kick_spin's own PPO sampling is currently frozen, see agent_plans/spin_implementation_plan.md section 0 -- its BC term still computes and is included in the kick group for consistency, but is zero-gradient until unfrozen) are scaled by kick_aux_coeff ('kick' group); tackle_attempt Bernoulli alone is scaled by tackle_aux_coeff ('tackle' group). Set aux_coeff_start/end=0.0 and kick_aux_coeff_start/end=1.0 (say) to train on kicking only for a round, independent of everything else -- same idea for tackle_aux_coeff.
bc._comment_bc_trains_frozen_heads: Whether the online BC-aux-during-PPO term (same Mode-3 term as _comment_aux above) still trains decision heads that PPOTrainer.set_frozen_heads() has frozen for the current curriculum phase (e.g. phase1_get_possession freezes shoot/pass/tackle/get_possession_raw/mark/hold_position -- see the 'PPO log_prob masking ACTIVE' log line for the live set). true (default, prior behaviour): BC keeps training them -- since only the head's OWN weights are frozen (requires_grad=False) while the shared decision_net trunk is not, this still backprops a demo-imitation pull into the shared trunk through those heads, on purpose, so the shared representation doesn't drift away from what those heads need even though PPO's reward has nothing to say about them this phase. false: PPOTrainer._bc_heads_for_loss() detaches exactly those heads' logits before computing the BC loss, so they get zero gradient from BC too -- fully inert until unfrozen, matching how PPO's own policy-gradient and entropy terms already treat them.
bc._comment_bc_pretrain_early_stop: Episode-leve1.15/15 train/val split + early stop for pretrain_combined()'s main BC epoch loop, mirroring value_pretrain_early_stop_patience/min_delta below. patience=0 (default) = disabled (no split computed, no early stop -- matches prior behaviour of training BC blind on the full dataset for exactly bc_pretrain_epochs). Set e.g. 3-5 to enable: patience = consecutive non-improving epochs allowed before stopping and restoring best-val weights; min_delta = minimum val BC-loss decrease to count as improvement. See 'BC val=' log line when enabled.
bc._comment_dec_exec_weight: Relative weight of decision-network vs execution-network losses in BC (pretrain and PPO aux annealing). dec=1.0/exec=1.0 = equal. Raise bc_exec_weight to push execution network (sprint, direction, tackle) harder; lower to let it drift more freely under RL.
bc._comment_combined_pretrain_rollout_steps: Steps to collect for the on-policy rollout used by pretrain_combined()'s joint BC + value warm-up (its rollout_steps= argument) when an offline --bc-dataset is supplied. Completely separate variable from value_pretrain_steps below (the standalone pretrain_value() fallback used when no dataset is given) — the two are never meant to share a value, tune independently. Also independent of ppo.rollout_steps (the main PPO rollout buffer size).
bc._comment_value_pretrain_batch_size: Minibatch size for pretrain_value()'s value-only fitting loop (and Phase 0's demo-return value warm-up inside pretrain_combined()). Worth tuning independently of ppo.minibatch_size and bc.bc_pretrain_batch_size -- those are sized for PPO's clip/KL-early-stop dynamics and BC's own convergence needs respectively, not necessarily right for a plain supervised value-MSE regression.
